name: Battle of Mycale

phases.title: The Greeks land and form two wings
phases.text: The Greeks landed out of sight of the Persian camp and formed two wings. The left stood from the shore to the foothills of the mountain, the right on the hills. The Persians had a palisaded camp with the fleet beached behind it.
phases.when: Afternoon of the same day as Plataea

phases.title: The Greek left meets the Persians alone
phases.text: The Persians came out of their camp and set up their shield wall. The Greek left began fighting while the right was still crossing the hills.

phases.title: The right comes up and breaks the shield wall
phases.text: The other Greek wing, under heavy arrow fire, chose to fight at close quarters and broke the wall by shoving. Tigranes and Mardontes died in the fighting.

phases.title: The Persians flee to their camp
phases.text: The Persians broke their lines and escaped to their camp. The Greek soldiers followed them in, and most of the Persian troops fled from the camp. The ethnic Persians grouped together and fought those who entered.

phases.title: The left outflanks the camp
phases.text: The Greek left arrived, outflanked the camp and fell on the rear of the Persians who remained, which completed the rout.

phases.title: The Milesians turn on the Persians
phases.text: The Milesians guarding the passes first misdirected the fleeing Persians, who ended up back among the Greek troops, and then began killing them.

phases.title: The fleet and fortifications are burned
phases.text: The Greeks burned the Persian fleet after a heavily contested fight with the Persian marines, once the loot had been taken from the ships and placed on the beach. The fortifications were burnt too.

note: The accounts say the Greeks probably formed two wings, and the Greek left and right are described in a way that does not fit together: the wing that fought first is called the left, but the wing that is then said to have broken the shield wall is called the right. This plan follows the order of events, with the Athenian-led wing first and the Spartan-led wing second. The accounts do not say where the camp and the beached fleet lay in relation to the hills, and they place the camp near the Gaison river without fixing the site; the camp, shore and passes are placed on the Persian side of the plan. Estimates of numbers vary widely and are not shown.
